clue.text: Sports venue, out of ballast mid-construction

indicators.note: construction means building something by putting parts together, so these letters are assembled afresh

parts.note: taken as written: the fifteen letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A new sports ground is going up, with ballast spilling out halfway through the works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid-construction' reads as halfway through the building work, but 'mid' belongs to the fodder: OUT OF BALLAST MID is what 'construction' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A ground where a team game is played in front of spectators.

clue.text: Sweet confusion

explanation.definitionFit: A soft toffee-like confection; also a muddle or an evasive botched compromise.

clue.text: Former pupil with assistant paying close attention

parts.note: OB, old boy, is a former pupil of a school
a servant is one who assists or attends on another

explanation.surface: An old boy and his helper are both watching keenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Watchful and quick to notice details.

clue.text: Bribe attendant to cover patrol route?

indicators.note: to cover says the two words conceal the answer, which runs across the gap between them

explanation.surface: Someone pays off a guard to keep the police patrol away.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles the end of 'Bribe' and the start of 'attendant'. The question mark flags a definition by example: a police officer's round.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer's regular round of streets is the area assigned to walk.

clue.text: Going to ground and hiding in the heather

indicators.note: hiding in says the word and is concealed within the plant name that follows

parts.note: ling is a common name for heather
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fox goes to earth, concealing itself among the moorland heather.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming down to earth from the air, as an aircraft does on arrival.

clue.text: Could carry rain right into position

indicators.note: into says the letter for right goes inside the word for position

parts.note: status means standing or position in society

explanation.surface: A forecaster warns that wet weather could move right into place.
explanation.definitionFit: A low, grey, even layer of cloud that often brings drizzle.

clue.text: A gathering to share worship

parts.note: a do is a party or social gathering
a ration is a fixed share or allowance

explanation.surface: Worshippers meet so that all may take part in devotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep love and reverence, as offered to a deity.

clue.text: Freezing bonus

explanation.definitionFit: Ice forming on surfaces such as aircraft wings; and, from 'the icing on the cake', a pleasing extra.

clue.text: Most powerful may lead, that is the way

indicators.note: lead says the first piece goes in front of the pieces that follow

parts.note: might is the past form of may, the modal verb of possibility
ie, id est, is the abbreviation for that is
St, short for street, is a way

explanation.surface: The strongest may take charge, and that is just how things go.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the greatest strength or force of all.

clue.text: Dad is turned in for contempt

indicators.note: turned means the letters of these two words are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A father has been reported to the police, which the family regards with scorn.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorn felt toward something thought unworthy.

clue.text: Smashed into rig, causing uproar

indicators.note: smashed suggests breaking apart, so the letters of these words are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Something crashed into an oil rig, setting off a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Running wild in violent public disorder makes a noisy tumult.

clue.text: Gain credit from introducing environmental and rural needs

indicators.note: introducing means the opening letters, the ones that introduce each word, are taken

explanation.surface: A politician wins praise by bringing in green and countryside policies.
explanation.definitionFit: To deserve or be paid something in return for work or merit.

clue.text: Drink on, one way to get agitated

indicators.note: on is read as taking on board, so the word for drink takes the other pieces into itself

parts.note: a draught is a single swallow of drink
I is the Roman numeral for one
St, short for street, is a way

explanation.surface: One more drink is a sure way to get someone worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Extremely upset and anxious, beside oneself with worry.

clue.text: Driving swine on the highway

parts.note: the words picture a pig loose on the road, but the swine is a selfish motorist who bullies others and takes more than a fair share of the lane

explanation.definitionFit: A reckless, selfish motorist who claims more of the lane than is fair.

clue.text: Wall covering rudimentary shed

parts.note: rough means crude or rudimentary
to cast is to shed, as a snake casts its skin

explanation.surface: A crude garden shed needs its walls rendered.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse plaster of lime mixed with gravel, used to render exterior walls.

clue.text: Advice note signed?

parts.note: the words suggest a signed letter of advice, but the signs are those of the zodiac: forecasts offering guidance for each star sign

explanation.definitionFit: An astrological forecast offering guidance according to star sign.

clue.text: Painting method, it's developed on behalf of the French

indicators.note: developed suggests something grown into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: pp, per procurationem, is written when signing a letter on someone else's behalf
le is French for the

explanation.surface: An artist explains that a new painting technique was developed for French patrons.
explanation.definitionFit: A technique of applying paint in many small dots or dabs.

clue.text: Cash left aboard at return of oil spill

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Cash left aboard at return of oil spill (9)': the wordplay is PORT (left aboard) + OF reversed ('return of') + OIL rearranged ('spill'), but 'Cash' does not define the answer; the blog and its commenter agree it is probably a misprint for 'Case'.
annotationWithheld.clue: Cash left aboard at return of oil spill

clue.text: Rock movement elevated, worth another look?

parts.note: up means raised or elevated

indicators.note: another look suggests the word is viewed again in a new arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A geologist decides a raised rock formation deserves a second inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: In geology, an upward shift of the strata on one side of a fault.

clue.text: Persuade leading well-heeled characters to change places

indicators.note: leading means the opening letter of the word well is taken
characters are letters, and changing places means the letters of heeled are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wealthy figures who swap roles find persuasion easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well-heeled' (rich) splits in two: 'leading' picks from the first half, and 'characters to change places' shuffles the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax someone with flattery into doing what you want.

clue.text: Building time ran out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: The construction project ran past its deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall slender tower attached to a mosque.

clue.text: Communications pioneer dropping model from romantic intrigue

indicators.note: intrigue suggests scheming and plotting, so the remaining letters are worked into a new order
dropping says the letter for model is removed from the word that follows

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous early car, so T stands for model

explanation.surface: A radio inventor walks out of an affair with a fashion model.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing T from ROMANTIC leaves ROMANIC, which 'intrigue' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian inventor who sent the first transatlantic wireless signals in 1901.

clue.text: Birds carry dead plant

parts.note: hawks are birds of prey
to bear is to carry
D is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Birds fly off carrying a dead plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow-flowered weed of the daisy family, genus Crepis.

clue.text: More sensible to get wires uncrossed

indicators.note: uncrossed suggests untangling crossed wires, so the letters are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: It is more prudent to keep electrical wires from crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: Having greater good judgment or prudence.

clue.text: Force back to a great distance

indicators.note: back means the letters for the force are read from right to left

parts.note: RAF, the Royal Air Force, is a military force

explanation.surface: An army is pushed back a long way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns RAF followed by A; the definition works as a noun, as in 'seen from afar'.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a noun in 'from afar': a remote place far away.

clue.text: Current resting place

explanation.walkthrough: In Orkney and Shetland the word names a strong tidal race, as in Sumburgh's, which makes 'Current' fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fierce tidal race in northern Scottish waters; also a perch where birds settle at night.

clue.text: Large bird camouflaged by tall grass or heather

indicators.note: camouflaged by means the bird is concealed within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A big bird hides itself in long grass or moorland plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A flightless South American bird resembling a small ostrich.

clue.text: Sailors' trick — first disembark, then sneak away

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor; plural ABS
a con is a swindle or trick

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of disembark is used

explanation.surface: Sailors play a trick: they go ashore first, then slip away.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee secretly, typically to avoid arrest.

clue.text: Title written into the Lloyd's register

indicators.note: written, as an entry is written in a ledger, says the title is set down within the words of the register entry

explanation.surface: A name is entered in the Lloyd's Register of shipping.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans 'into the Lloyd's'; 'register' completes the picture of a ledger in which the name is inscribed.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of Shakespeare's tragedy of the Moor of Venice.

clue.text: Trio's occupation, in book-craft

parts.note: a trio occupying a small vessel, and also the title of a comic novel about such a boating holiday

explanation.definitionFit: Jerome K. Jerome's 1889 comic novel about a boating holiday on the Thames.
